_doc: The hostile-server cases and the limits every SDK is held to, written once. hostile_node.py serves each case on its port; scenarios.sh hostile runs every driver's `host <id> <args>` against it; hostile_check.py reads this file to judge the result. The roster cases are served as a discovery server and judged on the `connect` event (`event`), since a client that cannot read the roster never connects. A limit is checked against the SDK's own constants (all six agree: a reply value of at most 2 MiB, a decompressed value of at most 64 MiB, a request that makes no progress for 30 s fails). The driver's own limit (scenarios.sh LIMIT, 90 s) is above every max_wall_s, so a call that never returns shows as `timeout`, not as a slow answer.
baseline_ceiling_note: peak_over_baseline_mib is the cgroup peak of the case minus the cgroup peak of the same SDK's `baseline` case, so a runtime's own footprint (JVM, .NET, Node) is not charged to the SDK. A driver that reports harness_floor_kb (its own threads in place, no SDK call yet) is judged against that instead.

cases.what: an honest node answers a get with a 1 KiB value
an honest reply (40 B value) arrives one byte every 100 ms: a slow but advancing peer must not be failed
the node completes the handshake, reads the request and never answers
the node sends `V 1000` and 10 bytes of the value, then goes silent
the reply declares a value of 2 MiB + 1 B (one over the reply cap) and sends all of it
the reply declares a value of 4294967295 B and sends none of it
a compress=true client gets a 1 MiB DEFLATE value that expands to 1 GiB

the node reads nothing after the handshake; 256 concurrent sets of 512 KiB (128 MiB handed to the client in all) share one buffer owned by the caller. A set may be sent again once on a new connection, so each of the two attempts gets the 30 s request timeout and the bound is 70 s
a discovery server answers the node list with `N 65537 2`: one node more than the SDKs accept (65536)
a discovery server sends entries of 64 KiB + 64 KiB without end: the response is capped at 16 MiB

a discovery server lists 128 nodes and none of them answers: every dial runs into its 5 s deadline, 64 at a time in five SDKs (two rounds, 10 s) and 16 at a time in Java (eight rounds, 40 s); a client that dials them one after the other takes 640 s
